reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004A9CB5 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/camera/004A9CB5-Camera_UpdateTransform_18.cpp at sha256 c52ec4e3dd260a9a152e6ea5a35198de5da0b9fad9f0efe69c683da37fa44949 (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t Camera_UpdateTransform_18(int32_t param_1);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

retail_function.name: Camera_UpdateTransform_18
retail_function.summary: Single block 0x4A9CB5-0x4A9CCB: EDX=[E+4]; EDX=(EDX&0x300)|0x7F; write the word to [E+6] (upper half of the caller's argument slot); fldcw [E+6]; retn. EAX is left untouched.

candidate_function.summary: __load_CW(int context) computes the same masked control word and writes it through `*(&context + 2)`, which is the caller's [E+6] word because `context` is the cdecl parameter at [E+4]; it then calls fldcw.

divergences: Return contract is not transcribed: retail leaves EAX untouched, while the candidate declares a non-void result and never returns a value (undefined EAX).
candidate_comparison.statement: Divergences are listed above; by contract they keep the record at TRANSCRIBED or lower.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.detail: Retail entry 0x004A9CB5 is recovered by all three tools; the address-bound implementation is scripts/GameNatives/camera/004A9CB5-Camera_UpdateTransform_18.cpp (sha256 c52ec4e3dd260a9a152e6ea5a35198de5da0b9fad9f0efe69c683da37fa44949). Single block 0x4A9CB5-0x4A9CCB: EDX=[E+4]; EDX=(EDX&0x300)|0x7F; write the word to [E+6] (upper half of the caller's argument slot); fldcw [E+6]; retn. EAX is left untouched. Candidate: __load_CW(int context) computes the same masked control word and writes it through `*(&context + 2)`, which is the caller's [E+6] word because `context` is the cdecl parameter at [E+4]; it then calls fldcw.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: Retail reads [E+4] and writes [E+6]; the candidate's single cdecl parameter sits at [E+4] and `&context+2` is exactly [E+6]. The stack frame matches.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.detail: One word at [E+4]; the candidate's `context` occupies the same slot and the write through its address reproduces the retail write to [E+6].

checks.name: control_flow_shape
checks.detail: Binary Ninja and radare2 agree on 1 blocks / 0 edges (similarity 1.000); angr CFGFast recovers 1 blocks with has_unresolved_jumps=false.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.detail: No calls in retail; the candidate's fldcw is the same x87 instruction.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.detail: The retail store to [E+6] and the candidate's `*(&context+2)` store target the same caller-owned word.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.detail: Retail never writes EAX, so the function returns the caller's EAX unchanged. The candidate declares `int` but has no return statement, so its EAX is undefined rather than provably preserved.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.detail: Both execute fldcw against the same computed word.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t(int32_t arg1)" at 0x004A9CB5; radare2 recovers "fcn.004a9cb5 (int32_t arg_4h, int16_t arg_6h);". Both tools place the entry at 0x004A9CB5 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: int32_t Camera_UpdateTransform_18(int32_t param_1);.

limitations: No game process was executed; this review is static (live Binary Ninja, radare2 CFG, angr CFGFast) plus the candidate source.
The candidate defines __load_CW, not the catalog name Camera_UpdateTransform_18.
